heading: multiview MV-3 — `evaluate`: an `extruded` solid whose profile has hundreds of points
text: Measured on the union that `solid3` builds for a prism (`unionPolygons([low, high, ...sweeps])`, one quad per profile edge) with a wavy curtain outline (0.08 m wide, 5 m long, swept 3 cm and 1.5 cm sideways; `🧰️matrix/MX-2/bench/prism-cost.ts`, same input for both modules, rings and area equal): polygon module of HEAD 4, 24, 80 and 271 ms for 40, 150, 400 and 764 points; live module (MM's engine of 17:48, landed by MX-2) 2, 4, 5 and 13 ms. The cost of a many-point prism per ring is therefore about 20 times lower at the size you measured (764 points); the quadratic growth of the old module (edge pairs of the slab union) is gone, the new one grows about linearly. Not measured: the willow itself (your prism trial is withdrawn; `prism.ts` rebuilds it) and a whole matrix of it. A prism whose profile is the drawn outline is what the README asks for a part that turns; with the new module it no longer needs the plates workaround for cost, and the plan of a curtain that swings could be a prism or, where its section changes along the bone, a `loft` (recipe in `multiview-MX-2.md`).
